correctness.rationale: The first-force lower bound \(Z(G)\ge\delta(G)\) is proved, and equality forces a minimum set to equal a closed neighborhood minus the forced neighbor. Each such set forces the complete closed neighborhood in one step, then grows a cyclic interval by explicit vertex forces. Near-complete cases are split and proved separately. The duplicate-count step uses exact intersections of length \(2k+1\) circular intervals and checks uniqueness. Connectivity follows by a single swap to a cyclic block, with a connected cyclic-block backbone. An independent explicit-neighbor and color-change enumerator verified 104 parameter pairs and 25 larger sample cases; the arbitrary theorem rests on the written proof, not that experiment.

value.rationale: The smallest number of initial active vertices is already known, but it alone gives neither solution multiplicities nor pathways between optimal configurations. Exact optimum counts, a first-force geometric classification for every power, and the contrast between complete, near-complete and regular regimes provide a motivated full census in a fundamental circulant family. Universal token-jumping connectivity is structurally substantive because zero-forcing reconfiguration graphs can be disconnected in general. These conclusions have applications to choosing or navigating equally-sized control/observation seed configurations without claiming a new scalar zero-forcing bound.
